Carry trades funded in low-yielders are vulnerable to further unwinding if the AI sell-off resumes, which could add volatility to Asian currencies, especially those tied to chip exports. A clearer Fed pause signal, along the lines JPMorgan's Kelly expects , would be the main thing that could ease the pressure on EM. articles.title: JPMorgan's Kelly: tech correction overdue, stocks to bounce, Fed to hike once then pause
articles.expand: Kelly's one-hike-then-pause view gives bulls a counter-narrative to the hawkish pricing that has weighed on stocks and gold. If December's statement or projections lean his way, front-end yields and the dollar could ease. Waller's push for 50bp, or a clear signal of a January follow-up, remains the main risk to that view. November CPI is now a key data point: a sizeable gasoline-driven drop would strengthen the case for a pause. Kelly's flow argument (401(k)s, buybacks, wealthy buyers) suggests dips may keep attracting support, even if the AI valuation debate isn't settled. --- Earlier: US sto...

articles.title: Ackman urges Fed to drop 2% inflation goal for 3%, warns 9 December hike risks recession
articles.expand: Ackman's post adds to a growing chorus, now including the Treasury, arguing against further Fed hikes. That could feed hopes of a softer message on 9 December even if the hike itself goes ahead. Rate markets are unlikely to shift much on investor commentary alone. Any sign that Fed officials are open to slowing the pace, though, would weigh on the dollar and front-end yields and support equities and gold. His SpaceX example also points to strain in credit markets, so corporate bond spreads are worth watching as a gauge of how much tightening is already in the system. --- Earlier: Could Nvidia ...

articles.title: SNB's Martin eyes second-round effects after inflation jumps to 1.5%, hike in view
articles.expand: Martin's focus on second-round effects is a hawkish signal, and it supports pricing for a December SNB hike. A tightening Swiss central bank alongside a hiking Fed changes the usual rate-differential story for the franc. Combined with strong safe-haven demand during the equity rout, that could keep the franc well bid, especially against the euro. That is the very currency risk Martin flagged, so the SNB may stay willing to lean against excessive franc strength even as it tightens. UBS shares remain exposed to headlines on the capital rules and any further talk of a headquarters move. --- Swiss...

articles.title: Australia flash PMI sinks to 46.1 as private sector shrinks at fastest pace in 5 years
articles.expand: A drop this deep, alongside the first easing in input cost inflation for months, weakens the case for further Australian monetary tightening. That leaves the Australian dollar exposed if rate markets start pricing a gentler path. The sharp fall in new export orders also points to softening external demand, at a time when global equities are already under heavy pressure. Prices are still running above their long-run averages, though, so policymakers are unlikely to move quickly to declare inflation beaten. Traders may also treat the flash reading cautiously until the final data in early Decembe...

articles.title: New Zealand retail volumes jump 2.2% in Q3, more than four times the expected pace
articles.expand: A beat of this size is supportive for the New Zealand dollar and should firm rate expectations at the margin, since it weakens the case that NZ consumers need more help. Any boost may be short-lived, though, with global risk appetite under heavy pressure after last week's Wall Street rout. A high-beta currency like the kiwi tends to follow broader sentiment in that kind of market. Liquidity is also thinner than usual with Tokyo closed , which can exaggerate the first move in either direction. ---- New Zealand consumers didn't just recover in the third quarter, they outran forecasts by a wide m...

articles.title: US equity rout: Bessent cautions Fed against overtightening, before its December decision
articles.expand: With a quarter-point hike in December close to fully priced, Bessent's comments mainly push back against the governors (well, one, looking at you Waller!) arguing for 50 basis points. They do little to dislodge 25bp as the base case. If the equity correction deepens, the bigger risk for rate markets is that a hold gets priced back in. For oil, the administration's argument depends on crude-driven inflation fading, so softer energy prices would strengthen Bessent's case and a new spike would back the hawks. Gold has tended to fall on rising hike expectations, so any easing of that pricing could...

articles.title: A December BoJ hike may not be enough: why a fuzzy endpoint keeps yen bears circling
articles.expand: With a December hike largely priced, the yen’s direction now hinges on the BoJ’s guidance beyond it. A vague statement or a cautious press conference from Ueda on December 18 risks a “hike and sell” reaction like last December’s. A clearer commitment to keep tightening toward 2% would give the yen more durable support. Until then, intervention risk near 160 is doing more to cap USD/JPY than rate expectations are. The July board changes add a longer-dated dovish tail risk that could weigh on yen forwards. --- The BoJ is agreed on December but divided on the destination, and that missing endpoin...

articles.title: Some analysts now see BoJ rates at 2.5% by mid-2027, despite slower underlying inflation
articles.expand: A 2.5% BoJ path is far from priced, so the forecast is more a marker of upside risk than a market mover. If the coming months show underlying inflation turning higher, front-end JGB yields would be the first to reprice, with the yen likely to follow. The view also raises the stakes for the BoJ’s December 18 statement and Ueda’s press conference, where any hint of a faster pace would carry weight. With energy and imported costs feeding producer prices, oil and USD/JPY remain the key inputs to watch. --- October’s slower underlying inflation hasn’t deterred the BoJ hawks: some forecasters now se...

articles.expand: The misses take a little edge off December hike pricing, but not enough to change the base case after Ueda’s hawkish remarks on Thursday. A slower underlying gauge leaves the yen with less support than it needed near 160, so the burden falls on intervention warnings rather than rate expectations. JGB yields may ease at the front end, but producer prices running at 7.1% keep the inflation pipeline full.
